subject: Social Habits
title: Show what we know
objectives: Children will show Term 1 learning through play stations.
Teachers will gather evidence for every child’s Term 1 record.
content: Revising greetings and manners, feelings and routines, and sharing and safety, with end-of-term records.
teachingActivities: Keep every activity familiar and joyful; observe quietly during play; record what children can do without pressure; share records with parents in plain language with a strength, a next step and a home idea.
learnerActivities: Show learning from the term through play stations and a celebration.
assessment: Observe and record each child’s Term 1 social learning.
expectedOutcomes: Completes familiar routines with growing confidence.
Each child has an observation record for Term 1.

lessons.title: Revising greetings and manners
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will revisit greetings, please, thank you and good manners through games.
successCriteria: Greets with a word or wave
Uses please and thank you with a prompt
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt about greetings, manners, feelings, routines, sharing, kindness, toileting and safety.
lessons.starter: Sing the greeting song and say "Today we play our favourite manners games."
teacherActivities: Play the door greeting game with the puppet.
Play the shop game with please and thank you.
Play the goodbye game with waves.
Let each child choose a favourite game.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play the door greeting game with the puppet. Children: Child greets the puppet.
Step 2. Teacher: Play the shop game with please and thank you. Children: Child asks and thanks.
Step 3. Teacher: Play the goodbye game with waves. Children: Child waves goodbye.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a favourite game. Children: Child chooses and plays.

practical.title: Manners games
steps: Children play each for four minutes.
practical.safety: Supervise each area and keep floors clear. Use large toys only.

differentiation.support: Play with the child and use one game.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead a game.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we say in the morning?

expectedOutcomes: Uses magic words with a prompt
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say thank you.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep using greetings and magic words at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit greetings, please, thank you and good manners through games" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?

lessons.title: Revising feelings and routines
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will revisit feelings, circle time, lining up and tidying through games.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt about greetings, manners, feelings, routines, sharing, kindness, toileting and safety.
lessons.starter: Show a feelings card and say "How do you feel today?"
teacherActivities: Play show me a feeling with the feelings cards.
Sit in the circle and sing the circle song.
Line up on footprints and walk.
Tidy up with the tidy-up song.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play show me a feeling with the feelings cards. Children: Child shows a feeling face.
Step 2. Teacher: Sit in the circle and sing the circle song. Children: Children sit and sing.
Step 3. Teacher: Line up on footprints and walk. Children: Children walk in a line.
Step 4. Teacher: Tidy up with the tidy-up song. Children: Children put toys in baskets.

practical.title: Feelings and routines games
practical.safety: Keep walkways clear and supervise each game. Stop any game that upsets a child.

differentiation.support: Play beside the child and name each feeling.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead the line.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do at tidy-up?

lessons.homeConnection: Talk about feelings and keep simple routines at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit feelings, circle time, lining up and tidying through games" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?

lessons.title: Social stations
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will gather evidence of each child’s Term 1 social learning at play stations.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt about greetings, manners, feelings, routines, sharing, kindness, toileting and safety.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we play at six stations and show what we know."
teacherActivities: Set up six stations: greetings, manners, feelings, sharing, kindness and hygiene.
Observe each child at two stations and record what they do.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up six stations: greetings, manners, feelings, sharing, kindness and hygiene. Children: Children rotate every three minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: Observe each child at two stations and record what they do. Children: Children play at stations.
Step 3. Teacher: Take photographs and make notes. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Social stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station with an adult or helper. Keep water shallow and floors clear and use only large toys.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and stay at familiar stations.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to show friends how a station works.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: greets; uses please and thank you; names feelings; shares and takes turns; shows kindness; washes hands.

expectedOutcomes: Shows familiar social skills at stations
lessons.conclusion: Say well done to everyone and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Play a favourite game at home during the holiday.

lessons.title: Revising sharing and safety
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will revisit sharing, taking turns, kindness and safety through games.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt about greetings, manners, feelings, routines, sharing, kindness, toileting and safety.
lessons.starter: Say "Let us build a tower together and be safe."
teacherActivities: Build a tower with blocks, taking turns.
Play stop and go with a stop sign.
Walk with the rope and count children.
Say a kind word to a friend.
learnerActivities: Child adds a block and waits.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Build a tower with blocks, taking turns. Children: Child adds a block and waits.
Step 2. Teacher: Play stop and go with a stop sign. Children: Children stop on stop.
Step 3. Teacher: Walk with the rope and count children. Children: Children walk with the rope.
Step 4. Teacher: Say a kind word to a friend. Children: Child says a kind word.

practical.title: Sharing and safety games
practical.safety: Use large, light blocks and keep floors clear. Supervise closely and keep a second adult at the rope walk.

differentiation.support: Take turns together with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to be the stop sign holder.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do with toys?
What do we do at stop?

lessons.conclusion: Count the children and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep practising sharing and safety rules at home.

lessons.title: Term celebration and records
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will celebrate Term 1 with songs, and teachers will complete each child’s Term 1 record.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt about greetings, manners, feelings, routines, sharing, kindness, toileting and safety.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we celebrate our term. Let us sing our favourite songs."
teacherActivities: Sing favourite songs and rhymes with actions.
Give each child a sticker and say their name.
Complete each child’s record and next step.
learnerActivities: Child waves and says thank you.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Sing favourite songs and rhymes with actions. Children: Children sing and do actions.
Step 2. Teacher: Give each child a sticker and say their name. Children: Child waves and says thank you.
Step 3. Teacher: Complete each child’s record and next step. Children: Children play quietly.

practical.title: Celebration circle
practical.safety: Check for allergies before any snack and use non-toxic stickers. Keep the floor clear and supervise all play.

differentiation.support: Hold the child’s hand and sing together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose the last song.

assessment.method: Complete each child’s Term 1 record from the term’s observations. Note a strength, a next step and a home idea for parents.

questions.question: What do you like to do?

lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say "See you next term."
lessons.homeConnection: Share the Term 1 record and keep practising manners over the holiday.
